conventions.convention: The Heisenberg algebra has n ≥ 1 and bracket [P_i,X_j] = δ_ij Z; its bracket is alternating even in characteristic 2.
W_n(k;ℏ) is the unital algebraic tensor-algebra quotient with [p_i,x_j] = ℏδ_ij 1; A_n(k) = W_n(k;1). No topology or exponential generators are included.
Normal ordering places all x generators before all p generators, with each family in increasing index order; exponents lie in ℕⁿ and include zero.
The trace lemma allows d = 0 and arbitrary commutative coefficient rings; the finite-dimensional obstruction requires characteristic zero, n ≥ 1, ℏ ≠ 0, and a nonzero unital representation.

The analytic bridge assumes AC and Countable Choice, finitely many self-adjoint generators, a common graph core invariant under every generator and every functional-calculus group, and orbit differentiability in every generator's graph norm.

For [A_a,A_b] = i c_ab I and U_a(s) = exp(isA_a), the pairwise phase is exp(-i c_ab st). The ordered-product W(f) includes exp((i/2)Σ_{a<b}c_ab f_a f_b), yielding phase exp(-iσ(f,g)/2). In the block-matrix case, the algebraic normalization is p_j = (i/κ)P_j on D.

load_bearing.statement: For a field k, n ≥ 1 and ℏ ∈ k, W_n(k;ℏ) is T(E_n) modulo the two-sided ideal generated by x_ix_j-x_jx_i, p_ip_j-p_jp_i, and p_ix_j-x_jp_i-ℏδ_ij1; A_n(k) = W_n(k;1).

For every field k, n ≥ 1 and ℏ ∈ k, W_n(k;ℏ) ≅ U(𝔥_n(k))/(Z-ℏ1), and the normal-ordered elements x^αp^β, α,β ∈ ℕⁿ, form a k-basis. If ℏ ≠ 0, scaling p_i ↦ ℏp_i gives W_n(k;ℏ) ≅ A_n(k); if ℏ = 0, the defining generators commute.
For a field k and n ≥ 1, 𝔥_n(k) has basis X_1,…,X_n,P_1,…,P_n,Z, bracket [P_i,X_j] = δ_ijZ and [X_i,P_j] = -δ_ijZ, with same-type and central brackets zero.

Under AC and Countable Choice, a finite self-adjoint family with real skew-symmetric scalar commutators on a common invariant graph core, invariant functional-calculus orbits, and the stated graph-norm differentiability satisfies U_a(s)U_b(t) = exp(-ic_ab st)U_b(t)U_a(s). Its specified ordered products W(f) are strongly continuous unitaries satisfying W(f)W(g) = exp(-iσ(f,g)/2)W(f+g) and W(f)* = W(-f). For the stated block matrix and κ ≠ 0, Q_j|D and (i/κ)P_j|D define an A_n(ℂ)-module.
Let R be a commutative ring, let d ≥ 0, and let A,B ∈ M_d(R). Then tr(AB-BA) = 0.
For every field k and integer n ≥ 1, the vector space and bracket specified in def-heisenberg-lie-algebra form a Lie algebra over k.

seams_checked.note: Read both page interfaces and the representation definition and module-equivalence proof. The prerequisite supplies compatible unital k-linear representation language. The Heisenberg page treats this as reading context and proves its actual algebra constructions from explicitly named suppliers; neither direction asserts automatic integration.

Read the regular-Weyl page and its universal-algebra definition's comparison. They distinguish bounded unitary symbols and representation regularity from polynomial generators, and do not import an unconditional exponentiation claim. The Heisenberg page and remark likewise leave universal completion and Stone–von Neumann uniqueness as separate obligations.

Read the Hall page and the normalized Jordan Fock-action theorem, including F4 and steps 2.1–3.1. Its finite-N actions use precisely [P_i,X_j] = δ_ijI, with commuting same-type generators and Z acting as identity. Infinite modes are handled through finite restrictions; no finite-dimensional module or analytic exponentiation claim is inferred.
